Shive is a powerful and spiritual name that represents the cyclical nature of life and the power of the universe.

It is a name that inspires reverence and awe, and is a powerful reminder of the divine presence within us all.
data.etymology: Shive belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Shiva, God of destruction and creation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shive total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.name: शिव
in_sanskrit.meaning: The Auspicious One, The God of Destruction and Creation
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root word 'shu' meaning 'that which is auspicious' and the suffix 'va' meaning 'the one who', Shiva is the name of the Hindu deity who is the embodiment of auspiciousness, the destroyer of evil and ignorance, and the creator of the universe. He is often represented with a third eye, a crescent moon on his forehead, and a serpent around his neck. Shiva is the supreme god in Shaivism, one of the major branches of Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Shiva is a major deity in Hinduism and is the supreme god in Shaivism, one of the major branches of Hinduism. He is the god of destruction and regeneration. The primary iconography of Shiva includes the third eye on his forehead, the crescent moon on his crown, and the serpent around his neck.
historical_references.context: Shiva is an important deity in ancient Indian religions, particularly Hinduism. His iconography and role have evolved over time, but he is consistently associated with destruction and regeneration.

historical_references.reference: Shiva is also known as Mahadeva (Great God), and is the supreme being in the Shaiva philosophy. He is represented as the destroyer of evil and the transformer. In contrast to Vishnu, who preserves the universe through his maintenance, Shiva destroys it in order to recreate it.
historical_references.context: During the medieval period, Hindu philosophies continued to evolve, and Shiva came to be seen as the supreme being in the Shaiva tradition. His destructive role was emphasized, and he came to be seen as the transformer of the universe.
